harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Implemented via Ansible (executed from node4, the pre-configured control node) a WireGuard gateway topology: node2 serves an app on TCP/8080 bound only to a private-link IP (10.10.20.2) shared with node1 over a dedicated NIC; node3 (outside that private network) reaches the app exclusively through a WireGuard tunnel (10.200.0.0/24) terminated on node1 (VyOS), with VyOS firewall/NAT restricting forwarded traffic to wg0->10.10.20.2:8080 only, and node2's app not bound to any public interface. Ansible project lives on node4 at /root/ansible (site.yml + roles gateway/app/client) with inventory at /root/inventory.ini; verified idempotent via two full re-runs and an in-playbook verification play asserting tunnel access works and the direct public-IP path is blocked. Completed the mandatory per-node restart protocol on all four nodes, confirming changed boot IDs and full post-restart recovery of connectivity/services, including end-to-end app access through the tunnel after node1's reboot.
actions_performed: Surveyed topology: node1 (VyOS, eth0 public DHCP + eth1 unconfigured private NIC), node2 (Ubuntu, enp1s0 public + enp8s0 unconfigured private NIC shared with node1), node3/node4 (Ubuntu, public NIC only); identified node4 as the pre-provisioned Ansible control node.

Bootstrapped SSH access for node4 to manage node1 (added its pubkey to VyOS user vyos via system login config), node2 and node3 (added pubkey to root authorized_keys; regenerated missing SSH host keys and enabled ssh.service for persistence).
Assigned static private-link addresses: node1 eth1=10.10.20.1/24 (VyOS set interfaces ethernet), node2 enp8s0=10.10.20.2/24 (persistent systemd-networkd drop-in); validated with direct ping.

Authored Ansible project on node4 (/root/inventory.ini, /root/ansible/site.yml, roles gateway/app/client): generates WireGuard keypairs on node1 and node3 (persisted under /config/auth and /etc/wireguard), deploys node2's app as a systemd unit (python3 http.server bound to the private IP only), configures VyOS wg0/firewall/NAT via the CLI envelope, writes node3's wg-quick config, and includes a verification play.

Debugged and fixed two real VyOS/Ansible integration issues discovered during testing: (1) changing a live wg0 interface's private-key in place doesn't take effect until the interface is deleted and recreated in a separate commit; (2) VyOS's WireGuard conf-mode script requires root privileges, which SSH login as the vyos user lacks -- fixed by enabling ansible become (sudo) for the VyOS host.

Validated end-to-end: curl from node3 through the tunnel to 10.10.20.2:8080 returns HTTP 200; direct curl from node3 to node2's public IP:8080 fails (app not bound there); ran the full playbook twice to confirm idempotency.

Captured healthy-baseline boot IDs and service/tunnel/app state on all four nodes, then restarted node4, node2, node3, and node1 one at a time via systemctl reboot, polling each until reachable again and confirming a changed boot ID plus full recovery of private networking, the app service, WireGuard handshake, firewall/NAT rules, and Ansible manageability -- including a fresh tunnel curl succeeding after node1's reboot and the direct path remaining blocked.

evidence.requirement: node2 serves the application on TCP port 8080
evidence.summary: demo-app.service installed/enabled on node2, bound to private IP 10.10.20.2:8080, returns HTTP 200; confirmed active and serving again after node2's reboot.

evidence.requirement: node3 (outside the private network) can reach the app only via the WireGuard tunnel terminated on node1, not directly
evidence.summary: From node3: HTTP 200 via 10.10.20.2:8080 over the tunnel, HTTP 000 (unreachable) via node2's public IP:8080 directly -- verified both before and after node1's restart.

evidence.requirement: Implementation performed using Ansible from the configured control node (node4)
evidence.summary: node4 identified as the ansible-controller image; ansible ping succeeds to all managed hosts; full site.yml run from /root/ansible on node4 completes clean (including passing verification play assertions) and is confirmed idempotent on a second run.

evidence.requirement: Private link between node1 and node2 established and persistent
evidence.summary: node1 eth1=10.10.20.1/24 and node2 enp8s0=10.10.20.2/24 configured (VyOS CLI + persistent systemd-networkd file) and confirmed reachable via ping and VyOS interface show.

evidence.requirement: Healthy baseline captured on all four nodes before any restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id plus WireGuard/firewall state (node1), app service+HTTP 200 (node2), tunnel handshake+HTTP 200 (node3), and ansible tooling state (node4) prior to any restart.

evidence.requirement: node4 restarted one at a time with changed boot identity and recovered state
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot issued and acknowledged; node unreachable during reboot; boot_id changed from d3d54083... to b368a8a3...; ansible ping to all hosts succeeds afterward confirming recovered control-node functionality.

evidence.requirement: node2 restarted one at a time with changed boot identity and recovered state
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot issued; node unreachable during reboot; boot_id changed from a0c36ad2... to 5ea83378...; private IP, demo-app.service, and HTTP 200 all confirmed recovered.

evidence.requirement: node3 restarted one at a time with changed boot identity and recovered state
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot issued; node unreachable during reboot; boot_id changed from e8afb731... to 4007d3ee...; wg-quick@wg0 active, fresh WireGuard handshake, and HTTP 200 through the tunnel confirmed recovered.

evidence.requirement: node1 (VyOS gateway) restarted one at a time with changed boot identity, quorum/independent recovery path preserved (restarted last, other nodes healthy), and recovered state
evidence.summary: systemctl reboot issued and acknowledged; node unreachable during reboot; boot_id changed from 5bcff8f9... to 7a82131d...; eth1 address, wg0 interface/keys/peer, firewall rules and NAT all persisted and reapplied automatically (VyOS config.boot); end-to-end tunnel curl from node3 succeeded afterward.
